item.title: Guest Speaker Dr. Springall
item.description:
Hello everyone,

Today’s meeting will be a fun one! We will be having Dr. Springall come give a guest lecture and demo. Dr. Springall teaches many of the courses here at Auburn that are relevant to ethical hacking and this demo will be a reflection of that. Interested in seeing ethical hacking primitives in action? Come join us!

Per usual this meeting will be in Shelby 3129

Hope to see you there!

item.title: Weekly Meeting 3/4: PicoCTF Practicum
item.description:
Hello everyone!

This week will be a fun interactive session where you get hands on experience with CTFs. The meeting will introduce PicoCTF which has a collection of puzzles that range from beginner friendly to very challenging. If you are looking for a space to try out puzzles while receiving guidance, stop by!

The meeting will start with a short intro by Luke and Brad (me), then will lead into practical demos and practice sessions.

item.title: SECCDC Results!
item.description:
Hello everyone, over this past weekend EHC participated in the South Eastern Collegiate Cyber Defense Competition (SECCDC) and achieved great results with a final placing of 11th out of 38.

According to the CCDC website the mission of the competition is to:

“provide institutions with an information assurance or computer security curriculum a controlled, competitive environment to assess their student’s depth of understanding and operational competency in managing the challenges inherent in protecting a corporate network infrastructure and business information systems.”

item.title: Weekly Meeting 11/19: Guest Speaker!
item.description:
Hello everyone, this week’s meeting will consist of a presentation my department professor Dr. Springall. The presentation will be a demonstration of a web-shell injection amongst other things, you won’t want to miss it!

Dr. Springall will also be discussing his new upcoming course COMP-5970 which will be an all-around course involving cyber security competitions. If you are interested in CTFs or other related competitions, we highly recommend you give it a look!

item.title: Competition Results!!! Cyber Force + NCL
item.description:
Hello everyone, EHC has great news!

Last weekend EHC sent a team to compete in the Department of Energy’s Cyber Force Competition in St. Charles Illinois. This event focusses heavily on defending systems from incessant attacks from a trained red team. Last year our team placed in 41st out of the roughly 90 teams, but this year we had a marked improvement and placed 15th! Congratulations to Luke, Marshall, Matthew, Hemant, Walker, and Jon on this stellar performance. Growths like these are what EHC strives to make on all fronts!

item.title: Weekly Meeting 9/3: Cyber Tools
item.description: This week we will continue with topics for people getting into cyber by introducing some relevant tools that are used in industry, education, and competitions. The meeting will be led collaboratively by Marshall, Luke, and Jon who will share their experiences and know-how when it comes to using some of these tools. If you are interested in participating in any of the events/competitions we will be hosting this semester, or if you are curious about what tools are relevant to previous competitions you have participated in, we highly recommend you attend.

item.title: CyberFire Puzzles 2024
item.description:
Hello everyone, we hope you had, or are having, a great summer. This year AUEHC will be opening up the fall semester with CyberFire Puzzles! This event is designed such that all skill-levels will find something engaging and will learn, so we highly encourage that you consider attending.

What is CyberFire Puzzles?

Created by the U.S. Department of Energy and Los Alamos National Laboratory , Cyber Fire Puzzles is a friendly competition that features a plethora of interesting mathematical and computer-science-based problems. You can expect to see sequence problems (think 1,5,9,d,…), number base conversion, network forensics, reverse engineering, and more. The problems in each category start at a beginner level but increase in difficulty as you learn from each problem.

item.title: Tracer FIRE 2023
item.description:
This past weekend (April 14-16), the Ethical Hacking Club and Sandia National Laboratory hosted a digital forensics and incident reponse (DFIR) competition called Tracer FIRE! Students from Auburn, Tuskegee, and Alabama State formed teams of 3-5 and collaborated with each other from Saturday morning through Sunday evening to find out what cyber attacks happened at a fictional company. More details about the competition below!

item.title: Kickoff Meeting And Kali
item.description:
In the first AUCTF meeting we went over the basics of what CTFs are, and then talked about the major suite of tools we use for competitions: Kali Linux.

What’s a CTF?

Cyber Security is one of the fastest growing career fields right now, but getting practice hacking things and figuring out new skills will lead to legal trouble if you do things you’re not supposed to, and get tedious due to the lack of competitive space. This is where Security Capture the Flags (CTFs) come in.
